comparisons.peer_summary: Effective in Q2 2024, JPMorganChase combined its former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking segments to form the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), resulting in three reportable segments: Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), CIB, and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), with remaining activities in Corporate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase disclosed significant strategic restructuring and segmentation changes during 2024 to align their business models. Goldman Sachs narrowed its focus on consumer-related activities, specifically mentioning the exit from certain consumer platforms like GreenSky and preparing for the Apple Card transition. JPMorgan Chase similarly reorganized its reportable segments by combining Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking into a single Commercial & Investment Bank segment, effectively altering its operational structure and reporting lines to reflect a changed strategic focus. While GS focused on divesting specific consumer assets, JPM focused on consolidating banking and investment functions into fewer, broader segments.

sentences.text: During 2023 and 2024, we narrowed our focus with respect to consumer-related activities by taking several actions.

See "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations - Regulatory and Other Matters - Other Matters - Narrowing our Focus on Consumer-Related Activities" for further information.

Effective in the second quarter of 2024, JPMorganChase reorganized its reportable business segments by combining the former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking business segments to form one reportable segment, the Commercial & Investment Bank.

As a result of the reorganization, the Firm has three reportable business segments - Consumer & Community Banking ("CCB"), Commercial & Investment Bank ("CIB") and Asset & Wealth Management ("AWM") - with the remaining activities in Corporate.
